name: triton_permuted_store_blocking_layout_pitfall
description: Fusing a permute into an upstream Triton kernel's store phase often LOSES vs a separate post-permute pass, because Triton's BlockedEncoding distributes threads along the outer tile axis first. Even `tl.trans(tile)` only swaps the LOGICAL tile axes — it doesn't change the PHYSICAL thread mapping. Stores to a layout where the inner (contiguous) dim differs from the tile's inner axis will be uncoalesced.
preconditions: Considering fusing a permute/reshape into a Triton kernel's output store
Target output layout has a DIFFERENT inner (stride-1) dim than the tile's natural inner axis
Source tile is produced with standard blocked layout (not explicit BlockedEncoding override)
steps: Profile the separate `kernel + post-permute` baseline BEFORE designing the fused version.
If the post-permute uses an LDS-tile Triton kernel that hits ~85%+ HBM peak, the fused version is unlikely to beat it.

If you still want to fuse, explicitly set the tile's BlockedEncoding to match the target output's inner axis. For gfx950 LDS 64-byte banks, aim for sizePerThread=[1,8] or [1,16] on the inner-matching axis.
Validate with CUDA event timing AND by checking the lane store pattern in AMDGCN dump (should see `buffer_store_dwordx4` with adjacent lanes at adjacent addresses).
expected_impact: Avoids 20-30% regression from naive fusion. In the HIP wgrad case: fused dual_jagged_permuted was 1301 us vs dual_jagged + fast_permute post-pass at 1092 us — 0.84× slower despite 30% less theoretical HBM traffic.
failure_contexts: 2026-04-24: implemented quant_mxfp8_dual_jagged_permuted to fuse the fp8 permute into the quant kernel for HIP wgrad. Bit-exact correctness but 20% slower than post-permute pipeline because thread layout distributed along outer axis (l) while permuted output wanted inner = m_local. tl.trans(xq_c) didn't help. Reverted (kept as docs-only reference).
decision_rules: Rule of thumb: if the post-permute kernel hits >= 80% of HBM peak, don't try to fuse — the layout penalty will beat you.
If fusing is still desired, use explicit BlockedEncoding overrides and AMDGCN-dump the stores.
A fused kernel with MORE total ops (quant + transpose) but the same HBM traffic IS still net-slower if any of its stores become uncoalesced.
